clips.note: They are tasting bottled water and he sees the price. He thinks it costs far too much for water.

clips.line: and I just thought that that was a rip-off for what it actually was.
clips.note: He paid $40 for one pizza. He thinks it wasn’t worth that much money.
around: especially in the last 10 years, is pizza.
I have definitely spent $40 for a pizza pie in the last year,
The only saving grace out of all of this is probably Costco.

clips.line: I think this is a total rip off.
clips.note: He thinks the price is much too high. “Total” makes it stronger: completely a rip-off.

clips.line: I got ripped off, ah, what a rip-off.
clips.note: He explains the word: you paid much more than something is worth. “I got ripped off” = someone took too much money from me.
around: Sometimes if things are way too expensive,
more expensive than they should be, you pay for that,

clips.line: They charge a lot and I think they’re a bit of a rip off.
clips.note: He talks about people who ask for a lot of money. He thinks they aren’t worth it. “A bit of” makes it softer.
